main_text.p: altitudinem Maris, & tempestas demerfit mea[?] Anatomen corporis libentissimè contuitus[?] ad inspiciendum (Adolescentes) quid iuvat conditoris tanti artificium, & operis tam stupendi fabricam? unde ὠδὴ ... illud antiquorum ex parte constat, oculis perlustrare & admirari? Corpori tantum opera impendatur, & nihil animae? Hujus desiderabitur, & non Alterius Anatome? At quid cogitata adeo evisceret & in apricum protraheret, Hypocrisis larvâ detraheret, cordator ut obrizum e fornace defecatiores educeret, ac Tentationum (quibus perpetuò colluctamur) ignis purgatorius? Ut in Bello fortis, sapiens in ira, amicus in adversis praecipuè eminet; Ita in acrioribus tentationum paroxismis, examen subit, & se probat, generosum pectus. Siquidem attolle oculos ad Deum, quàm proclives sumus prosperis intumescere, & in depressis animum despondere? Demittas deinde ad terrestrem glebam, caro statim titillat, mundus lenocinatur, & Diabolus 1.Pet.5. ὡς λέων ὠρυόμενος περιπατεῖ 1.Pet.4. ζητῶν τινα καταπιεῖν[?], tanquam Leo rugiens agit peripateticum quaerens quem devoret, sive absorbeat. Thesauros Beneficentiae effundit in nos caelestis pa-ter?
Pf. 139. Arab. Adag. 50. Ps. 139. 1. Pet. 4. 1. Pet. 5.

page.notes: Left margin notes: "Pf.139." beside "toris tanti artificium"; "1.Pet.4." beside "bulcum perpetuò"; "Arab.Adag. 50." beside "in aduerfis"; "1.Pet.5." beside "Leo rugiens". The Greek fragments and some marginal references are small and partly blurred; the Greek is a best reading. Words marked [?] are doubtful. The line "ὠδὴ ..." is a partly unreadable Greek word and should be checked against the scan. Italic words are read from the scan and may be inexact. The first paragraph continues from the previous page; the last word is hyphenated across the line end ("pa-ter?").
